practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional learner maps time to the January 2026 ABIM ACHD blueprint. Which major category has the largest typical percentage?

options.text: Embryology and Anatomy (4%)
Noninvasive Diagnostic Testing Indications and Interpretation (20%)
Reproductive Health (5%)
Life and Health Management (5%)

practiceQuestions.rationale: The published blueprint assigns 20% to noninvasive diagnostic testing, the largest listed major category. It is a study map, not a prediction of a particular exam form.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement accurately describes the ABIM Training Pathway minimum?

options.text: 12 months total with no clinical-month requirement
24 months total ACHD fellowship including 18 months full-time clinical training
24 months of independent self-study
A procedure log only

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM lists 24 total months and 18 clinical months, with no required procedures in its table. Other prerequisites, competence and policy requirements remain.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has tetralogy of Fallot repaired in childhood. In the 2025 ACHD anatomic classification, which category is assigned to TOF?

options.text: I: Simple
II: Moderate Complexity
III: Great Complexity only if symptomatic
Not included

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2025 guideline lists TOF under moderate complexity. Physiological stage is assessed separately, so anatomy alone does not determine current status.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult with Fontan circulation is discussed in seminar. Which reflects a 2025 guideline top take-home message?

options.text: No liver surveillance if asymptomatic
At least annual liver imaging and laboratory evaluation including AFP, plus at least one hepatology consultation
Fontan is simple CHD
No ACHD input is needed

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AHA summary describes annual imaging/laboratory evaluation including AFP and at least one hepatology consultation. Real surveillance is set by the ACHD/hepatology team.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with a systemic right ventricle develops atrial arrhythmia. Which statement best reflects the 2025 summary?

options.text: Rate control is always preferred
Rhythm control is typically preferred over rate control in complex patients such as systemic RV or Fontan
Anatomy never affects rhythm strategy
Online study can select antiarrhythmics

practiceQuestions.rationale: The summary states rhythm control is typically preferred in the cited complex contexts. It does not authorize individual treatment selection.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional person with ACHD asks whether every dental visit requires antibiotics. What is the most accurate learning response?

options.text: All congenital lesions need antibiotics
No congenital lesion ever needs prophylaxis
Some highest-risk people may be recommended antibiotics before specified dental procedures; clinician determines applicability
Oral health is irrelevant

practiceQuestions.rationale: AHA frames prophylaxis as conditional for highest-risk people and specified dental procedures, and emphasizes oral health. Exact eligibility/medication requires the treating team.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional preconception conference for ACHD, which statement is best?

options.text: All require cesarean delivery
Most ACHD pregnancies can undergo vaginal delivery safely with appropriate risk stratification and monitoring
Anatomy/physiology are irrelevant
An online course grants pregnancy clearance

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AHA summary says “most” and adds risk stratification/monitoring; it is not a universal delivery rule.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult with moderate-complexity ACHD needs a noncardiac procedure. What principle is most consistent with the guideline summary?

options.text: CHD anatomy never changes procedural planning
An ACHD cardiologist should be involved to guide procedure, anesthesia and postprocedure care
Only primary care should be involved
No review needed if well

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AHA summary recommends ACHD cardiologist involvement for moderate/complex ACHD procedures. The actual plan remains clinical work.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional applicant is certified only in general internal medicine and completed online ACHD study. Which prerequisite is explicitly listed by ABIM?

options.text: Prior ABIM cardiovascular disease or ABP pediatric cardiology certification
Any online course
A minimum YouTube viewing time
Radiology residency

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM requires prior ABIM cardiovascular-disease or ABP pediatric-cardiology certification plus training/licence/competence/exam requirements. This course supplies none.

title: Advanced Cardiovascular Disease Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship — generic core category; independent self-study only-aligned independent study
prerequisites: MD/DO-level medical knowledge or comparable supervised postgraduate clinical background; this is not an entry-to-medicine course.
Prior knowledge of internal-medicine history/examination, basic pharmacology, ECG vocabulary, biostatistics and informed-consent/shared-decision principles.
Access to local supervision for any clinical image, ECG, procedure, medication, or patient-specific question.
For restricted datasets, individual compliance with the owner’s current terms; no data download, rehosting or re-identification through this course.
objectives: Organize cardiovascular presentations using the May 2026 ABIM Cardiovascular Disease blueprint.
Interpret publicly available educational material using structured uncertainty statements and appropriate supervision boundaries.
Synthesize current, openly readable guideline messages for chronic coronary disease, heart failure, AF, valve, aortic and PAD domains.
Distinguish the core Cardiovascular Disease category from separately named advanced Hopkins programmes and ABIM subspecialty certifications.
Appraise evidence, equity, systems and patient-goals considerations without providing individual treatment advice.

units.title: Cardiovascular foundations, prevention, risk and equity
objectives: Integrate history, examination, risk factors and social context into a problem representation.
Apply evidence appraisal and shared decision-making concepts to prevention and chronic cardiovascular disease.
Recognize health-equity and adherence issues as clinical and systems domains, not patient deficits.
boardDomains: Systemic Disorders Affecting the Circulatory System (4%)
units.casePractice: Use only synthetic risk-vignette values; compare preventive reasoning with the 2023 CCD guideline. Do not generate a patient-specific risk prescription.
units.assessment: Annotated evidence appraisal: identify a claim, population, outcome, limitation and equity consideration in one public guideline recommendation.

units.title: Rhythm, ECG and arrhythmia reasoning
objectives: Use a reproducible ECG description sequence before naming a rhythm.
Relate symptoms, structural disease and reversible contributors to arrhythmia differential diagnosis.
Distinguish a board-blueprint interpretation skill from invasive EP procedural competence.
units.casePractice: Use only a non-identifying schematic tracing or a lawfully linked public teaching trace; learners document rhythm description, differential, and urgent-feature reasoning without diagnosing a real person.
units.assessment: Five-item tracing-description drill plus one short reflection on how device-detected AF differs from a treatment order.

units.title: Acute coronary syndromes and myocardial injury
objectives: Separate acute myocardial infarction phenotypes and myocardial injury conceptually.
Build a time-sensitive differential for chest discomfort with ECG, biomarker and hemodynamic context.
Identify mechanical complications as escalation problems requiring team-based care.
units.casePractice: Fictional serial-ECG/troponin timeline: state what additional context would change the differential. No real ECG or management order is supplied.
units.assessment: One single-best-answer item and a two-column distinction table: ischemic mechanism versus nonischemic injury.

units.title: Chronic coronary disease, ischemia and revascularization
objectives: Organize chronic coronary disease around symptoms, functional change, risk and guideline-directed therapy.
Explain why anatomy, physiology, comorbidity and goals matter in a Heart-Team discussion.
Recognize that a new test is not automatically indicated in a stable patient without clinical change.
units.casePractice: Fictional chronic-symptom comparison: extract missing data before discussing a testing/revascularization framework.
units.assessment: Guideline-to-vignette critique that cites the 2023 CCD take-home message on routine periodic testing.

units.title: Heart failure, cardiomyopathy and advanced therapies
objectives: Differentiate HFrEF, HFmrEF, HFpEF and HF with improved EF at a conceptual level.
Relate hemodynamics, phenotype and comorbidity to congestion/perfusion reasoning.
Recognize when advanced HF, MCS or transplant discussion requires a specialty team and goals-of-care framework.
units.casePractice: Use Sunnybrook CMR labels only as a retrospective learning set; identify the data label, modality limits, and what clinical context is absent. Do not treat a dataset label as a bedside diagnosis.
units.assessment: Phenotype map plus a 600-word advanced-HF referral/goals-of-care discussion for a fictional scenario.

units.title: Valvular, pericardial and endocardial disease
objectives: Describe a valve problem by symptoms, anatomy, severity, ventricular/pulmonary response and concordance of data.
Identify when discordance prompts additional noninvasive or invasive evaluation rather than a premature conclusion.
Explain why multidisciplinary valve evaluation and shared decision-making matter for intervention choices.
units.casePractice: Link to EchoNet-Dynamic only under its individual research-use agreement. Practice view identification and limitation statements—not patient diagnosis—from an allowed training file.
units.assessment: Structured imaging report template: view, chamber/valve finding, uncertainty, corroborating data, and escalation question.

units.title: Hypertension, aortic and peripheral vascular disease
objectives: Classify aortic, arterial and venous presentations and identify high-risk features.
Explain imaging measurement, surveillance and team-based aortic care principles.
Use ABI and symptom context in an educational PAD diagnostic framework.
topics: PAD, claudication, CLTI, acute limb ischemia
units.casePractice: Fictional aortic-measurement trend: calculate a change rate, then state which details (method, body size, syndrome, symptoms) are required before guideline application.
units.assessment: Short answer: distinguish surveillance reasoning from an intervention recommendation.

units.title: Pulmonary circulation, thromboembolism and right heart
objectives: Differentiate PE, pulmonary hypertension groups and right-ventricular failure as overlapping but nonidentical syndromes.
Interpret the role and limits of hemodynamics and imaging in a pulmonary-circulation differential.
Recognize care escalation and contraindication-sensitive decision points without performing procedures.
units.casePractice: Fictional dyspnea case: build a differential and specify what imaging/hemodynamic evidence would be required.
units.assessment: Two-branch concept map: thromboembolic versus pulmonary vascular mechanisms.

units.title: Congenital, cardio-obstetric and systemic cardiovascular disease
objectives: Relate repaired congenital anatomy to adult circulatory physiology and acquired disease.
Recognize cardio-oncology and pregnancy as contexts requiring coordinated specialty input.
Avoid importing nuclear-medicine/theranostic claims into a core cardiovascular fellowship scope.
boardDomains: Systemic Disorders Affecting the Circulatory System (4%)
units.casePractice: Fictional adult-congenital transition vignette: identify anatomy, physiology, acquired comorbidity and referral questions.
units.assessment: One-page multidisciplinary communication note for a fictional transition-of-care scenario.

units.title: Multimodality imaging, angiography and hemodynamics
objectives: Select a question-driven modality rather than treating imaging modalities as interchangeable.
Use a standard description sequence for ECG, echo and coronary angiographic findings.
State the limits of independent viewing and the need for supervised clinical image interpretation.
units.casePractice: Use Sunnybrook CC0 CMR only as an authentic de-identified image-learning source; retain provenance and do not claim CMR establishes a diagnosis alone.
units.assessment: Three structured reports from public/schematic material: modality, key observation, uncertainty, and question for a supervisor.

units.title: Critical care cardiology, MCS and transplantation
objectives: Frame shock by perfusion, congestion, etiology and trajectory.
Explain at a high level the purpose and limitations of temporary/permanent MCS and transplantation.
Use ethical, palliative and shared-decision principles in advanced disease discussions.
units.casePractice: Fictional shock timeline: categorize perfusion/congestion evidence and list team members required; no device selection or treatment order.
units.assessment: Team-based oral case presentation evaluated with a rubric for uncertainty, goals and systems factors.

units.title: Evidence, safety, quality and longitudinal professional practice
objectives: Appraise guideline scope, evidence limits and conflicts of interest.
Communicate uncertainty and reduce inequities in longitudinal cardiovascular care.
Separate knowledge rehearsal from the documented competencies and procedures required for certification.
boardDomains: All published ABIM domains; health equity may be included
units.casePractice: De-identified/public only: audit a fictional follow-up pathway for access, adherence and safety risks.
units.assessment: Capstone evidence memo with a transparent uncertainty statement and source audit.

topicGaps: The ready lecture set is rich in advanced topical Grand Rounds but is not a systematic beginner sequence for ECG interpretation, echocardiographic view acquisition/measurement, or coronary-angiogram reading.

No free public recording found in this verified ledger substitutes for observed supervised procedures, image overread, cath-lab participation, overnight call, continuity clinic or team-based assessment.
Core blueprint areas are discussed unevenly by the Grand Rounds format; use the readings and planned topic clips for sequencing, but planned clips are not ready content and carry zero verified hours.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.programmeSourceScope: CATEGORY, not a separately named programme: the declared “Advanced Cardiovascular Disease Fellowship” resolves to Johns Hopkins’ core Cardiovascular Disease Fellowship Program. practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with chronic coronary disease has no new symptoms and no functional decline after optimization of preventive therapy. Which statement best matches the 2023 ACC/AHA chronic coronary disease guideline?

options.text: Schedule periodic anatomic or ischemic testing solely for routine risk stratification.
Routine periodic anatomic or ischemic testing without a clinical or functional change is not recommended to guide treatment.
Use a beta blocker indefinitely for outcome improvement regardless of prior MI, LVEF, or another indication.
Advise nonprescription fish oil as a substitute for evidence-based secondary prevention.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline’s take-home messages state that routine periodic anatomic or ischemic testing without a change in clinical or functional status is not recommended for risk stratification or therapeutic decision-making. This is a knowledge item, not an individual care recommendation.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional learner is matching the 2022 HF guideline’s foundational HFrEF medication classes. Which set is correct?

options.text: ARNI/ACEi/ARB, evidence-based beta blocker, MRA, and SGLT2 inhibitor.
Loop diuretic, nitrate, digoxin, and aspirin only.
Calcium-channel blocker, alpha blocker, nitrate, and aspirin only.
Statin, fibrate, niacin, and omega-3 supplement only.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2022 guideline identifies four medication classes in HFrEF GDMT, including SGLT2 inhibitors. Selection, contraindications, dosing, monitoring, and patient-specific decisions require clinical supervision.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional scenario asks how to frame stroke-prevention discussion for atrial fibrillation. Which approach best reflects the 2023 AF guideline?

options.text: Use only a single score and ignore annual risk, AF burden, or shared decision-making.
Base discussion on estimated annual thromboembolic risk using a validated clinical score, and consider risk modifiers when uncertainty remains.
Use a bleeding score as the only determinant of stroke risk.
Treat all device-detected episodes identically regardless of duration or baseline risk.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline uses annual thromboembolic risk with validated clinical scores and allows additional risk modifiers when a patient is intermediate risk or uncertain. This item does not authorize an anticoagulation decision.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has atrial fibrillation and a mechanical prosthetic valve. Which anticoagulant class is identified in the 2020 valvular guideline take-home messages for this context?

options.text: A vitamin K antagonist.
A non–vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulant in all circumstances.
No antithrombotic therapy because the valve is prosthetic.
Antiplatelet therapy alone as a universal substitute.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline distinguishes rheumatic mitral stenosis or a mechanical prosthesis with AF, for which it states a vitamin K antagonist should be used. Individual therapy is outside this curriculum.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional surveillance dataset shows a sporadic ascending aortic aneurysm growing 0.5 cm over one year using comparable measurements. Which statement matches the 2022 aortic-disease guideline definition cited in its take-home messages?

options.text: This rate is never relevant to intervention discussions.
Rapid growth can be defined as at least 0.5 cm in one year for sporadic aneurysms.
Only a single absolute diameter can ever be considered.
All patients have the same threshold regardless of body size or heritable disease.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline defines rapid growth for sporadic aneurysms as ≥0.5 cm in one year or ≥0.3 cm/y in two consecutive years, with distinct qualifiers for heritable disease/BAV. This educational item is not a surgical threshold recommendation for a person.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement accurately describes the ABIM May 2026 Cardiovascular Disease imaging component blueprint?

options.text: ECG 48%, echocardiograms 37%, coronary angiograms 15%.
ECG 15%, echocardiograms 48%, coronary angiograms 37%.
Echo and angiography are excluded from the exam blueprint.
The blueprint substitutes for supervised image-interpretation competency.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABIM blueprint assigns 48% ECG, 37% echocardiograms, and 15% coronary angiograms to its image component. The blueprint tests knowledge/interpretation; it does not grant clinical credentialing.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with advanced HF wishes to prolong survival despite persistent high-risk disease. What systems-level step is emphasized in the 2022 HF guideline take-home messages?

options.text: Avoid referral to a specialized HF team until all options are exhausted.
Refer to a HF specialty team to review management, assess advanced-therapy suitability, and use palliative care consistent with goals.
Use only isolated procedural volume to determine all care.
Treat palliative care as incompatible with survival-focused goals.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline emphasizes referral to an HF specialty team for patients with advanced HF who wish to prolong survival, including review of therapies and goal-concordant palliative care.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has PAD and is not at increased bleeding risk. Which statement is included in the 2024 PAD guideline take-home messages?

options.text: Low-dose rivaroxaban 2.5 mg twice daily plus low-dose aspirin is effective to prevent major adverse cardiovascular and limb events in appropriate patients.
Full-intensity oral anticoagulation plus antiplatelet therapy is universally beneficial for PAD.
Structured exercise has no role in PAD care.
ABI is never used in PAD detection.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline states that this low-dose combination is effective in PAD patients who are not at increased bleeding risk, while treatment selection remains individualized.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional learner summarizes the 2020 valve guideline. Which feature should be included in a severe valvular disease intervention discussion?

options.text: Evaluate the patient with a multidisciplinary team, with referral or consultation with a primary or comprehensive valve center.
Ignore symptoms and ventricular response once an imaging number is available.
Use transcatheter treatment for every valve patient without a team evaluation.
Treat physical examination and initial imaging discordance as irrelevant.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline’s take-home messages call for multidisciplinary evaluation for severe valve disease considered for intervention and for further evaluation when clinical and initial noninvasive data are discordant.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best captures the certification boundary for this independent course?

options.text: Completing the 36-hour lecture ledger grants ABIM eligibility.
A self-study course can substitute for the documented clinical months and procedures of fellowship.

ABIM cardiovascular certification requires prior ABIM internal medicine certification, qualifying fellowship training, competence documentation, a valid unrestricted license, and passing the examination.
Attendance at postgraduate courses can be credited automatically toward subspecialty certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM’s current policy lists these general requirements and specifies 36 months of training, 24 clinical months, and required procedures. It also says postgraduate course attendance is not creditable toward certification requirements.

title: Cardiothoracic Surgery Fellowship

prerequisites.level: Advanced postgraduate surgical knowledge; designed as independent, non-credit study for physicians, trainees, and appropriately supervised health professionals.
requiredKnowledge: Medical-school anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pathology, and clinical epidemiology.
General-surgery-level perioperative assessment, sterile technique, informed-consent principles, and interpretation of standard imaging and laboratory data.
Ability to read clinical practice guidelines and explain uncertainty, alternatives, and multidisciplinary decision-making.
notProvided: No operative permission, simulator sign-off, entrustment decision, patient-care authorization, case log, supervision, clinical rotation, license, or credentialing.
Learners without prior surgical training should use the material only for conceptual learning and must not attempt invasive procedures or make patient-specific treatment decisions.

objectives: Map a clinical problem to the ABTS public written and oral domains without claiming access to protected examination content.
Construct a multidisciplinary, patient-centred preoperative problem representation that distinguishes indication, anatomy, physiology, risk, and goals of care.

Explain the conceptual components and safety checks of cardiopulmonary bypass, myocardial protection, perfusion, and mechanical circulatory support while deferring operational actions to supervised teams and local protocols.
Compare evidence-guided options for coronary, valvular, and aortic disease using guideline scope, patient factors, and Heart/Aortic Team decision-making.
Stage and evaluate thoracic disease conceptually, including lung, pleural, mediastinal, esophageal, airway, chest-wall, and diaphragmatic presentations.
Recognize perioperative deterioration patterns and articulate escalation, communication, and systems-safety principles rather than performing unsupervised intervention.
Interpret authentic de-identified, licensed lung CT/PET-CT datasets only within their stated research labels, provenance, and licensing constraints.
Present a structured oral-case response covering selection, work-up, preparation, operative strategy at a high level, postoperative surveillance, complication response, and evidence limits.

objectives: Differentiate the Hopkins directory label from the public programme-site label.
Map broad learning to ABTS’s approximately equal cardiac and general-thoracic written domains and its six-plus-six oral-case structure.

units.casePractice: Write a one-page scope statement for a fictional referred patient, identifying which decisions require a Heart Team, thoracic tumour board, attending surgeon, perfusion, anaesthesia, or critical-care team.

units.title: Preoperative reasoning, risk, imaging, and team planning
objectives: Build a problem representation from symptoms, anatomy, physiology, imaging, and patient goals.
State why risk scores inform but do not replace shared multidisciplinary judgment.
units.casePractice: Use the Lung-PET-CT-Dx landing page and a fictional clinical vignette to identify what the dataset labels establish and what they cannot establish about individual resectability.
units.assessment: Submit a structured five-minute fictional tumour-board or Heart-Team presentation with explicit uncertainty and no treatment order.

units.title: Perfusion, myocardial protection, and extracorporeal support concepts
objectives: Diagram the conceptual inflow, pump/oxygenator, heat exchange, outflow, monitoring, and safety roles in bypass.
Explain why local perfusion and anticoagulation protocols, direct supervision, and checklists are indispensable.
units.casePractice: Annotate a conceptual bypass diagram and list role-dependent stop points; do not calculate doses or simulate a clinical pump run.
units.assessment: Short-answer safety reflection and labelled diagram.

units.title: Coronary revascularization and surgical decision frameworks
objectives: Explain why anatomy, feasibility, comorbidity, medication considerations, goals, and patient preference belong in a Heart-Team decision.
Contrast guideline-informed indications with an automatic procedure rule.
units.casePractice: For a fictional left-main-disease referral, list the data a Heart Team needs and the patient-centred questions to ask; do not choose an intervention from this exercise alone.
units.assessment: One original multiple-choice item plus rationale citing the guideline.

units.title: Valves, rhythm, and structural heart disease
objectives: Frame symptomatic severe valve disease in terms of indication, anatomy, procedural suitability, longevity, risk, and preference.
Explain why SAVR versus transcatheter decisions are individualised rather than determined by one age or risk threshold.
units.casePractice: Create a fictional valve-team decision grid that keeps symptoms, imaging severity, procedural feasibility, frailty, anatomy, durability, and patient values as separate variables.
units.assessment: Oral-case rehearsal scored for problem representation, uncertainty, and safe escalation—not technical performance.

units.title: Aortic disease and cerebral/spinal protection principles
objectives: Differentiate acute aortic syndromes conceptually and describe the role of a multidisciplinary aortic team and timely expert transfer.
Explain the purpose and limits of perfusion, cannulation, neurological, and spinal-cord protection strategies at a conceptual level.
topics: acute type A and type B dissection
units.casePractice: Use a fictional acute-aortic-transfer scenario to identify time-critical communication, information transfer, and team roles. It is not a protocol for real emergency care.
units.assessment: Guideline-to-case mapping with citations and a limitation statement.

units.title: Lung, airway, and thoracic oncology
objectives: Organise a lung-mass evaluation around diagnosis, staging, physiology, multidisciplinary review, and patient goals.
Distinguish an imaging-label dataset from a diagnosis, stage, or operative indication.
units.casePractice: Linked-only review of TCIA Lung-PET-CT-Dx under CC BY 4.0; cite its DOI, preserve dataset labels, do not re-identify, and do not use the research images for clinical diagnosis.
units.assessment: A de-identified fictional staging worksheet with a provenance and licence field.

units.title: Pleura, mediastinum, chest wall, diaphragm, and esophagus
objectives: Develop a differential and work-up plan for pleural, mediastinal, chest-wall, diaphragmatic, and esophageal presentations.
Describe postoperative surveillance and complication recognition at a high level.
units.casePractice: Discuss a fictional pleural-sepsis case using assessment, source control concepts, multidisciplinary coordination, and escalation thresholds; no drainage or procedural instruction is supplied.
units.assessment: Four-station written case comparison.

units.title: Congenital, transplant, mechanical support, and critical care
objectives: Describe the public Hopkins exposure areas without claiming an individual rotation or competence.
Recognise why congenital, transplant, VAD/ECMO, and ICU care require specialty-team pathways.
units.casePractice: Create an escalation map for a fictional postoperative decline, naming team roles and information needs rather than prescribing therapy.
units.assessment: Structured handoff and systems-safety critique.

units.title: Quality, evidence, oral-case communication, and synthesis
objectives: Use guideline currency, study provenance, and licensing as explicit parts of clinical reasoning.
Deliver a concise oral response that covers selection, preparation, high-level strategy, surveillance, complication recognition, and uncertainty.
units.casePractice: Record a five-minute response to one fictional cardiac and one fictional thoracic prompt; label it practice, not an ABTS simulation or passing predictor.
units.assessment: Capstone evidence-and-communication portfolio.

assignment.title: Two-track evidence portfolio
requirements: A cardiac-track fictional case summary (1,000 words maximum) using a current primary guideline, a patient-values section, and a stated escalation boundary.
A general-thoracic fictional case summary (1,000 words maximum) using an authentic TCIA resource only by link/DOI, a data-provenance note, and no copied or rehosted image.
A three-minute structured oral response for each track, explicitly stating uncertainty, team roles, and why it does not direct care.

mapping.institution: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine / The Johns Hopkins Hospital
mapping.name: Cardiothoracic Surgery Fellowship (directory label); Cardiothoracic Surgery Residency Program (programme-site label)
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: The directory page lists ACGME accreditation, The Johns Hopkins Hospital, a three-year duration, and training following a surgical residency. It says year 1 is divided between red and blue cardiac services; year 2 balances general thoracic service with a local elective in thoracic, cardiac, or endovascular surgery; and year 3 is chief cardiac surgery on red/blue services. The programme overview gives a more granular, partly variant description: year 1 adult cardiac, congenital cardiac, and thoracic; year 2 thoracic and adult cardiac with mechanical circulatory support, ECMO and transplantation plus elective opportunity; year 3 chief adult cardiac with possible thoracic time. The public 2023 booklet lists year 1 congenital/thoracic/adult cardiac/TAVR, year 2 VAD/ECMO/transplant/TVT and thoracic chief, year 3 adult-cardiac chief. These are institutional descriptions, not an independent course rotation and not a guarantee for any individual trainee.

medical.boardStatus: ABTS primary certification is one certificate in thoracic surgery. ABTS publishes cardiac and general-thoracic content matrices and operative pathways, but does not describe a separate board certificate called ‘cardiothoracic surgery fellowship.’
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent course neither confers nor establishes ABTS board eligibility. ABTS states that Board Eligible means an approved application is on file. Its certification pathways require specified ACGME/Canadian/integrated training routes, satisfactory ABTS examinations, acceptable ethical standing, an unrestricted US jurisdiction medical license at application/certification (with the stated in-training exception), and operative experience. For a three-year programme ABTS lists 375 major cardiothoracic cases (125 annually); those cases and supervision cannot be obtained, logged, substituted, or validated here. The current candidate must verify requirements, application timing, staging edition, and eligibility directly with ABTS.

officialProgrammes.institution: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine / The Johns Hopkins Hospital
officialProgrammes.name: Cardiothoracic Surgery Fellowship (directory label); Cardiothoracic Surgery Residency Program (programme-site label)
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: The directory page lists ACGME accreditation, The Johns Hopkins Hospital, a three-year duration, and training following a surgical residency. It says year 1 is divided between red and blue cardiac services; year 2 balances general thoracic service with a local elective in thoracic, cardiac, or endovascular surgery; and year 3 is chief cardiac surgery on red/blue services. The programme overview gives a more granular, partly variant description: year 1 adult cardiac, congenital cardiac, and thoracic; year 2 thoracic and adult cardiac with mechanical circulatory support, ECMO and transplantation plus elective opportunity; year 3 chief adult cardiac with possible thoracic time. The public 2023 booklet lists year 1 congenital/thoracic/adult cardiac/TAVR, year 2 VAD/ECMO/transplant/TVT and thoracic chief, year 3 adult-cardiac chief. These are institutional descriptions, not an independent course rotation and not a guarantee for any individual trainee.

medical.programmeSourceScope: This is an actual, separate ACGME-accredited three-year Johns Hopkins training programme, not a generic directory category. The supplied directory calls it the ‘Cardiothoracic Surgery Fellowship’; its linked public programme site calls the same three-year programme the ‘Cardiothoracic Surgery Residency Program.’ This entry transparently studies the combined adult cardiac, general thoracic, selected congenital-cardiac, mechanical-circulatory-support/transplant, perioperative, and critical-care knowledge domain of that programme. It does not create a second programme, a separate cardiac-surgery certificate, or an institutional affiliation.
sourceCaveats: The supplied user outline is nuclear-medicine/radiology material and is out of scope for this cardiothoracic-surgery entry; its unsupported volume, dual-board, and modality claims were not imported.

Johns Hopkins public directory and programme pages use different labels for the same three-year programme. The evidence supports a real programme, but not a distinct additional fellowship or a separate certificate.

The Hopkins booklet is publicly accessible but is branded 2022/2023 and may not describe every current assignment. The current directory and programme pages are primary sources for identity and summary; programme leadership is the authority for live details.
ABTS pages are board sources, ACGME pages are training standards, and institutional pages are programme descriptions. They are not interchangeable and do not confer affiliation or eligibility.

Some free videos are historic and must not be used as current clinical guidance without cross-checking the cited guideline. Age-restricted recordings were not counted. Transcript-terminal time is a conservative observed lower-bound method, not a guessed playlist duration.
TCIA research images are authentic and de-identified but not clinical consultation material. Observe licence, citation, no-reidentification, and no-rehosting/mirroring constraints.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner says completion of this independent course makes them ‘ABTS board eligible.’ Which correction is most accurate?

options.text: Board eligibility follows from completing any 36-hour course.
ABTS uses ‘Board Eligible’ for an individual with an approved application on file; training, licensure, operative and examination requirements remain separate.
The Hopkins directory title automatically grants an ABTS certificate.
ABTS has no training-pathway requirements.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABTS’s initial-certification page defines Board Eligible as having an approved application on file. Its pathways and operative requirements remain applicable; independent study cannot establish them.

practiceQuestions.stem: Under the ABTS operative-requirements page, what major-case total corresponds to a three-year programme?

options.text: 125 total
250 total
375 total, based on 125 major cardiothoracic cases annually
No volume requirement is published

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABTS lists 125 major cardiothoracic operations per year, 375 total, for three-year programmes. This course cannot provide or validate those cases.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which description best matches the public ABTS written-examination blueprint?

options.text: Only adult cardiac surgery is tested.
Cardiac and general thoracic are each approximately half of the examination, with published subdomains.
It contains only oral scenarios.
It is exclusively a technical-skills test.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABTS publishes approximate 50% cardiac and 50% general-thoracic composition, alongside component ranges. The page describes a 250-question cognitive written examination.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional oral-case rehearsal, which structure best reflects the public ABTS oral blueprint?

options.text: Name a procedure immediately and omit uncertainty.
Address selection, diagnosis/staging, preoperative preparation, high-level intraoperative reasoning, and postoperative/complication planning in both cardiac and thoracic contexts.
Focus only on imaging interpretation.
Use leaked prior cases.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABTS says each protocol may test those elements and that the examination includes six general-thoracic and six cardiac scenarios. This question uses an original fictional rehearsal, not ABTS content.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has significant left-main coronary disease and an unclear optimal revascularization strategy. What is the most defensible study-level principle?

options.text: Choose a modality based only on age.

Use a multidisciplinary Heart Team and patient-centred decision-making; the guideline identifies surgical revascularization as indicated to improve survival relative to medical therapy for significant left-main disease.
Ignore anatomy and patient preference.
Make a decision from a single online video.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI guideline’s take-home messages support Heart-Team, patient-centred decisions and state the survival indication for surgical revascularization in significant left-main disease. Actual treatment requires clinical evaluation.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement is consistent with the 2020 ACC/AHA valve guideline for a fictional symptomatic patient with severe high-gradient aortic stenosis?

options.text: Valve intervention is never considered.
AVR has beneficial effects on survival, symptoms, and LV systolic function; selection of SAVR versus transcatheter intervention must be individualised.
One chronological age mandates a single approach for all patients.
Shared decision-making is unnecessary.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline supports AVR in symptomatic severe high-gradient AS and describes individualised choice of SAVR versus TAVI based on factors including anatomy, risk, expected longevity, durability, and values.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional clinically stable patient is suspected of having acute type A aortic dissection. Which source-grounded systems statement is best?

options.text: An online learner should select an operative technique immediately.
The 2022 ACC/AHA guideline supports considering transfer to a high-volume aortic centre and multidisciplinary care; real-time management belongs to emergency and specialist teams.
No imaging review is needed.
Family history is irrelevant.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline’s top messages address high-volume centre transfer for clinically stable acute type A dissection and multidisciplinary teams. It does not turn an independent learner into an emergency decision-maker.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which handling of the TCIA Lung-PET-CT-Dx collection is permitted by the course case-practice rules?

options.text: Rehost images without attribution and infer a real person’s identity.
Use the linked CC BY 4.0 collection for research-style study, cite its DOI, preserve provenance, and never attempt re-identification or clinical diagnosis from it.
Present the annotations as an operative indication for a new patient.
Ignore its licence because it is free to view.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The collection lists CC BY 4.0 and TCIA requires citation and prohibits re-identification. Dataset labels and annotations do not provide real-patient treatment advice.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement most accurately describes the Johns Hopkins programme in this record?

options.text: It is only a generic category with no identified programme.

It is an ACGME-accredited three-year programme; directory and programme-site labels differ, and public rotation descriptions should be presented as institutional information rather than replicated clinical training.
It grants an extra ABTS cardiac certificate.
Its public case log is a universal minimum for all learners.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The supplied directory lists an ACGME-accredited three-year Cardiothoracic Surgery Fellowship. The programme site calls it a residency programme and describes related rotations; neither source makes independent learners trainees or grants a separate certificate.

practiceQuestions.stem: Why are the 23.080833 verified video hours reported separately from the 36-hour target?

options.text: Planned clips and clinical rotations can be counted immediately.
Only deduplicated, publicly reachable recordings with observed durations are counted; planned clips, unknown durations, and age-restricted recordings are not counted as ready lecture hours.
Every web page is assumed to be one hour.
Duration is irrelevant to a video curriculum floor.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The contract requires observed accessible recording durations and prohibits padding. The exact ready-hour shortfall is therefore reported rather than concealed.

boardNames: American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) — Cardiovascular Disease Certification Examination
medical.boardStatus: ABIM offers a distinct Cardiovascular Disease certification examination. “Cardiovascular Medicine Fellowships” is BIDMC’s directory category, not a board certificate, combined fellowship or standalone ABIM eligibility category.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Independent study cannot establish eligibility. ABIM states that, at application, candidates must already be ABIM-certified in Internal Medicine; complete qualifying ACGME/Canadian cardiovascular disease fellowship training; demonstrate clinical/procedural competence and professional behavior; hold a valid unrestricted, unchallenged medical licence; and pass the examination. ABIM lists 36 training months, 24 clinical months and specified supervised competencies/procedures. Courses, videos, research, postgraduate courses, practice experience and category-page review cannot provide this credit. Confirm personal eligibility directly with ABIM.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The exact declared BIDMC page is a generic Cardiovascular Medicine Fellowships directory/category. It links to one actual core Cardiovascular Disease Fellowship plus separate advanced fellowships. This entry transparently studies the adult general CVD knowledge scope aligned to the ABIM CVD blueprint. BIDMC advanced imaging, structural heart, cardio-oncology, outcomes research, clinical electrophysiology, clinical hypertension, interventional cardiology and vascular medicine are distinct variants; they are orientation/survey material here, never combined training tracks or inferred certifications.
sourceCaveats: The declared MED-021 title is a BIDMC directory category. Scope is general adult CVD; no broad certificate, combined advanced fellowship or affiliation is invented.

The supplied user outline concerns nuclear medicine/radiology, theranostics and imaging claims. It is out of scope and was not imported; no nuclear-medicine certification, radiopharmaceutical, scan or Emory/Harvard imaging-track claim is made here.
Public Yale recordings are not BIDMC lectures, ABIM products, a complete board review or proof of CME. Free access is playback access, not reuse permission.
ABIM sample cases are protected; this course links to them only and creates original questions.
Guidance evolves; sources were checked 2026-10-07. This is not a treatment guideline or patient-specific advice.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional examinee is planning the CVD ECG/imaging component. Under the May 2026 ABIM blueprint, which modality has the largest stated share?

options.text: Coronary angiograms (48%)
Electrocardiograms (48%)
Echocardiograms (48%)
Coronary CT angiograms (48%)

practiceQuestions.rationale: The published component allocates 48% to ECGs, 37% to echocardiograms and 15% to coronary angiograms. A blueprint weight is not a prediction of an individual test.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult has exertional chest discomfort and known chronic coronary disease in outpatient follow-up. Which framing matches the 2023 CCD guideline?

options.text: It replaces acute-ACS emergency protocols for every patient.
It addresses chronic outpatient evaluation, symptom relief, future-event reduction and revascularization decisions after stabilization.
It applies only after bypass surgery.
It excludes microvascular angina.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline’s scope is chronic outpatient CCD, with diagnostic evaluation, symptoms/QOL, prevention of future events and revascularization decisions after acute stabilization; it includes vasospasm or microvascular angina.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional AF review, which is explicitly a major section of the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS guideline?

options.text: Prevention of thromboembolism
Routine prophylactic coronary stenting
Nuclear thyroid ablation technique
Pediatric congenital surgical repair only

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline includes thromboembolism prevention, rate control, rhythm control, risk-factor modification and special patient groups. This asks about document scope, not an individual anticoagulation decision.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has a short PR interval and delta wave on a 12-lead ECG. Which ABIM sample-case principle is most appropriate?

options.text: Call the delta wave a diagnostic lateral MI Q wave without context.
Describe a pre-excitation/WPW pattern and avoid a contradictory MI label based on the delta wave.
Assume the tracing proves structural cardiomyopathy.
Ignore conduction findings because ECGs are not scored.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM’s public sample explanation notes that delta waves can mimic Q waves and that a contradictory lateral-MI selection invalidates the WPW-pattern answer.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional learner selects one PTB-XL waveform for a descriptive exercise. Which practice follows the stated terms?

options.text: Repost it without credit because the data are public.
Use it with CC BY 4.0 attribution for educational description, without relying on it for patient care.
Attempt to identify the patient from age and shifted dates.
Treat a dataset label as definitive clinical diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.rationale: PTB-XL is open access under CC BY 4.0 and pseudonymized. Attribution is required; re-identification is improper; dataset labels do not establish bedside diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has HCM and a family-history question. Which topic is explicitly covered by the 2024 HCM guideline contents?

options.text: Genetics and family screening
Mandatory universal bypass
Radiopharmaceutical thyroid dosing
Treatment of all congenital lesions as the same condition

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline includes diagnosis, imaging, rhythm assessment and genetics/family screening. It does not determine management for a real individual.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult has lower-extremity symptoms and concern for PAD. Which statement represents the 2024 PAD guideline scope?

options.text: Only pediatric congenital arterial disease
Atherosclerotic/thrombotic lower-extremity PAD across asymptomatic, chronic symptomatic, CLTI and acute limb ischemia presentations
Only venous varicosities
Only thoracic aortic dissection

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline covers assessment, testing, therapy, exercise, revascularization and follow-up for lower-extremity PAD subsets. It does not replace urgent evaluation of limb-threatening symptoms.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional echo report describes severe MR after acute ischemic symptoms. What is the safest learning response?

options.text: Use a still frame to prescribe a procedure independently.
List observed findings, identify missing clinical/Doppler information and recognize urgent supervised assessment may be needed.
Label every posterior leaflet as vegetation.
Ignore symptoms because valve disease is imaging-only.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM sample cases emphasize significant findings actually shown and clinical context. The valvular guideline distinguishes diagnosis/follow-up, therapy and intervention; neither source authorizes independent care.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional course planner claims online lectures equal an ACGME cardiovascular fellowship. Which correction is accurate?

options.text: ACGME programme length is measured only in online hours.
ACGME requires a 36-month programme with competency-based experiences, progressive responsibility, supervision and structured activities beyond patient care.
It is correct after 36 video hours.
It is correct after sample cases.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2026 ACGME requirements specify 36 months and clinical educational structures that self-study cannot supply. Video is a curriculum floor, not clinical-training time.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional physician seeks ABIM CVD certification after self-study. Which additional requirement is explicitly stated by ABIM and cannot be supplied here?

options.text: Unrestricted licence, qualifying accredited fellowship, documented competence and the examination
Playlist completion badge only
Social-media video response
Any nonclinical webinar

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM requires prior IM certification at application, qualifying training, competence, valid unrestricted licence and the certification exam. This curriculum supplies none of these eligibility elements.

title: Clinical Cardiac Electrophysiology Training Program
prerequisites: MD/DO-level cardiology knowledge or equivalent advanced-health-professional background; this is not an entry-level ECG course.
Working knowledge of cardiovascular anatomy, 12-lead ECG, pharmacology, hemodynamics, and guideline reading.
For de-identified datasets: ability to follow the resource licence, preserve attribution, and avoid attempting re-identification.

No learner may use this course to perform invasive testing, ablation, CIED implantation/programming, extraction, medication selection, or patient-specific triage. These require local policy, supervision, credentials, and patient care setting.
objectives: Map learning to the January 2026 ABIM CCEP content categories without representing this course as ABIM preparation or an official exam resource.
Interpret rhythm data and state what it can and cannot establish.
Compare mechanism-based concepts across bradycardia, SVT, atrial arrhythmias, ventricular arrhythmias, inherited syndromes, and devices.
Appraise current guideline scope and explain uncertainty, shared-decision, safety, and referral boundaries.
Use authentic, de-identified, licensed ECG data lawfully for educational pattern-recognition practice.

units.title: Cellular EP, anatomy, and antiarrhythmic reasoning
objectives: Relate ion currents, refractoriness, autonomic inputs, and anisotropy to triggered activity and re-entry.
Interpret how pharmacokinetics and use/reverse-use dependence alter an antiarrhythmic rationale without selecting treatment for a real patient.
Recognize inherited-channel and structural substrate questions that require specialist/genetic evaluation.
boardDomains: Basic Physiology, Anatomy, Pharmacology, and Genetics (20%)
units.casePractice: Use PTB-XL only to identify waveform features and label uncertainty; no treatment recommendation.
units.assessment: 10-item mechanism-to-tracing matching quiz plus a cited concept map.

units.title: Surface ECG, ambulatory monitoring, and symptom–rhythm correlation
objectives: Distinguish a rhythm observation from a symptom–rhythm correlation and state data limitations.
Apply a structured approach to wide-QRS rhythm differential diagnosis and artifact recognition.
Select monitoring questions that would change a differential in a fictional case, rather than ordering tests for a real person.
units.casePractice: Compare de-identified PTB-XL ECG statement labels with a learner interpretation; document discordance and confounders.
units.assessment: Timed tracing annotation with a one-paragraph evidence/uncertainty note.

units.title: EP study, intracardiac electrograms, mapping, and procedural safety
objectives: Describe what intracardiac recordings, programmed stimulation, activation mapping, pace mapping, and entrainment are intended to test.
Identify signal-quality, reference, windowing, and fusion pitfalls.
Explain why transseptal/pericardial access and ablation require supervised institutional practice, not online replication.
units.casePractice: Use the public lecture diagrams for note-taking only; do not reproduce patient screenshots or perform maneuvers.
units.assessment: Annotated fictional electrogram strip: identify reference, timing relationship, and one limitation.

units.title: SVT mechanisms: AVNRT, accessory pathways, and junctional tachycardias
objectives: Construct a mechanism-based differential for a regular narrow or wide tachycardia in a fictional scenario.
Compare AVNRT, orthodromic/antidromic AVRT, and atrial tachycardia using atrial/ventricular timing concepts.
State why an observed maneuver supports but may not prove a mechanism.
units.casePractice: Create a fictional EP-lab reasoning table; no procedural targets or energy settings.
units.assessment: Five original single-best-answer mechanism questions and a one-minute verbal explanation.

units.title: Ventricular ectopy, VT, and sudden-death substrate reasoning
objectives: Localize only at a conceptual level from a 12-lead PVC/VT morphology and state uncertainty.
Compare idiopathic, ischemic-scar, and nonischemic VT substrate reasoning.
Describe the roles and limitations of imaging, monitoring, and risk stratification in a fictional case.
units.casePractice: Use MIMIC-IV-ECG or PTB-XL waveform records only under their licences; label all conclusions as educational hypotheses.
units.assessment: Cited VT/PVC substrate worksheet; a risk statement must distinguish evidence from inference.

units.title: VT mapping and ablation strategy—concepts, limitations, and complications
objectives: Explain activation, substrate, entrainment, and pace-mapping concepts without treating them as interchangeable.
Contrast ischemic and nonischemic VT ablation challenges, including hemodynamic tolerance and epicardial considerations.
Identify why procedural imaging, team readiness, and complication management cannot be replaced by a recording.
units.casePractice: Write a non-actionable map-interpretation critique from a public lecture; no simulated catheter procedure.
units.assessment: Two-page comparison of mapping strategies, including one failure mode for each.

units.title: Atrial fibrillation and flutter: integrated longitudinal reasoning
objectives: Organize AF care questions into risk-factor modification, stroke-risk assessment, rate/rhythm strategy, and follow-up.
Distinguish typical CTI-dependent flutter from atypical macroreentry conceptually.
Explain why LAAO, ablation, and antithrombotic choices need individualized, guideline-based and supervised decisions.
units.casePractice: Draft a fictional shared-decision question list, not a treatment plan, and map it to the 2023/2025 guidelines.
units.assessment: Guideline-navigation exercise that identifies source section and uncertainty for three fictional AF scenarios.

units.title: Bradycardia, syncope, pacing, and CRT/physiologic pacing
objectives: Build a differential for bradycardia or syncope and identify reversible-cause and symptom-correlation questions.
Compare conventional pacing, CRT, and conduction-system/physiologic pacing concepts at a high level.
Interpret why a device indication, programming choice, or return-to-play decision cannot be made from an online course alone.
units.casePractice: Use fictional timelines to decide what additional information is missing before attributing syncope to a rhythm.
units.assessment: Structured syncope reasoning note with a monitoring limitation and referral/escalation boundary.

units.title: ICDs, follow-up, remote data, lead complications, and extraction boundaries
objectives: Describe ICD, wearable/subcutaneous options, interrogation, remote monitoring, and follow-up concepts.
Recognize infection, malfunction, vascular, and recall/advisory questions that require urgent specialist pathways.
Explain why lead extraction requires an appropriately equipped centre, experienced team, and surgical backup.
units.casePractice: Review a fictional device alert and identify information to verify; do not recommend reprogramming or extraction.
units.assessment: Safety-focused escalation map with no procedural instructions.

units.title: Inherited syndromes, cardiomyopathy, congenital disease, pregnancy, and athletes
objectives: Recognize long-QT, Brugada, CPVT, HCM, ARVC, sarcoid, and cardiomyopathy as distinct substrates with different uncertainty and referral needs.
Describe how congenital anatomy, pregnancy, and athletic participation change the question set.
Use shared decision-making language while avoiding clearance or return-to-play determinations.
units.casePractice: Use a fictional family-history pedigree with no genomic result disclosure or real-patient counselling.
units.assessment: Syndrome-to-referral-and-evidence matrix.

units.title: Evidence appraisal, safety culture, equity, and systems practice
objectives: Appraise a guideline recommendation’s scope, evidence date, and applicability limits.
Identify consent, conflict-of-interest, radiation/occupational, reporting, and team-based safety issues.
Explain how equity and access can affect monitoring, follow-up, and shared decisions without stereotyping a patient.
boardDomains: All domains; ABIM notes clinically important health-equity content may be assessed
units.casePractice: Appraise a public guideline landing page for date, sponsoring body, and decision boundary.
units.assessment: One-page evidence brief plus conflict/limitation declaration.

units.title: Capstone: integrated non-procedural EP reasoning
objectives: Synthesize physiology, ECG/monitor data, imaging context, device data, and guideline scope in a fictional vignette.
Communicate uncertainty, safety-netting, and the limit of independent study.
Separate knowledge assessment from procedural competence, board eligibility, and licensure.
units.casePractice: Capstone uses only fictional composite cases plus linked lawful data resources, not patient records.
units.assessment: Capstone written synthesis and oral presentation scored with an educational rubric, not a credentialing decision.

assignment.title: Evidence-bound CCEP capstone (independent-study plan)
deliverables: A 1,500–2,000 word analysis of one fictional composite rhythm scenario using an original schematic or a linked lawful waveform—not a rehosted image.
A table separating observed facts, differential hypotheses, missing information, applicable guideline/source, and escalation/supervision boundary.
A licence and attribution statement for any dataset consulted.
A two-minute recorded or written explanation of why the analysis is not a treatment plan or procedural competency claim.
assignment.constraints: No real patient record, protected examination material, proprietary teaching image, procedural simulation, drug dose, procedure recommendation, clearance decision, or copied slide may be submitted.

topicGaps: Verified open recordings now total 22.318333 h, still 13.681667 h below the 36-hour floor; this is an observed-duration ledger, not rendered hours or training equivalence.

New recordings improve AF/flutter, tachyarrhythmia ECG interpretation, and inherited-syndrome coverage. No newly verified long-form recording closes the gaps in antiarrhythmic pharmacology, bradycardia/syncope reasoning, pacing/CRT/CIED follow-up, EP signal fundamentals, or safety/equity systems.

The residual 13.681667-hour requirement is not feasible to claim as completed from the public recordings verified in this pass. Topic-specific production plans are not proof that authoritative source-supported narration can be expanded to that length without repetition; require editorial/clinician validation and another search for authentic full-length recordings.
Supervised case responsibility, clinic follow-up, live EP laboratory experience, device implantation/programming, procedural logs and attestation remain non-substitutable.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardNames: American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) — Clinical Cardiac Electrophysiology (CCEP) Certification Examination
medical.boardStatus: ABIM offers a distinct CCEP subspecialty certification examination. ABIM’s January 2026 public CERT blueprint—not Johns Hopkins, ACGME, or this independent course—defines the stated examination content categories.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Independent study does not confer eligibility. As of the ABIM policy checked 2026-10-07, initial CCEP certification requires prior ABIM certification in cardiovascular disease at application; acceptable formal training; demonstrated competence; a valid unrestricted, unchallenged medical license; and passing the CCEP examination. For fellows beginning in/after AY 2017–18, ABIM specifies 3 years cardiovascular disease fellowship (including 24 clinical months) plus 24 months CCEP training and documented procedure expectations (160 ablations with stated subtype minima, 100 CIED implantations, 30 replacements/revisions, 200 interrogations/programming events, and 5 tilt-table tests). Training must be acceptable/accredited as stated by ABIM. Procedure numbers do not guarantee proficiency; programme director attestation and all current policies apply. This course supplies none of these requirements.

officialProgrammes.institution: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine / Johns Hopkins Medicine
officialProgrammes.name: Clinical Cardiac Electrophysiology Training Program
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Actual standalone, 2-year ACGME-accredited CCEP fellowship. The detailed public programme page describes participation in inpatient/outpatient Arrhythmia Service care; increasing supervised EP-lab responsibility; diagnostic EP, mapping, SVT/VT ablation, pacemaker/ICD/CRT implantation, lead extraction, LAAO, cardioversions, tilt/device tests; a weekly ambulatory clinic day rotating through faculty and device clinic; weekly EP service meeting/journal club/research; and Johns Hopkins Hospital/Outpatient Center with Bayview opportunity. It states fellows are supervised in all clinical activities, not that online viewers may perform these activities.

medical.programmeSourceScope: This discovered entry is an actual separate CCEP fellowship, not a generic directory category: Johns Hopkins’ directory identifies it as 2 years and ACGME-accredited, and the linked programme page gives a CCEP-specific curriculum. Scope is transparent: this independent curriculum uses the public description only; it does not claim unpublished rotations, case volume, equipment access, trainee status, affiliation, or accreditation. There is one supplied institutional variant; no duplicate Harvard/Emory or research-only entry is merged into it.
sourceCaveats: Johns Hopkins’ public programme description is an institutional curriculum description, not a complete rotation schedule, case log, or published didactic-hour ledger.
ABIM policy, ABIM blueprint, ACGME milestones, and Johns Hopkins programme pages have different functions. The course does not equate them.

The supplied user outline concerns nuclear medicine/radiology rather than CCEP and includes unsupported claims outside this entry’s scope; none was imported as CCEP curriculum, rotation, certification, or case-volume evidence.
Guidelines are date-checked through 2026-10-07, but future updates may supersede them. Sources are educational references, not personalized care instructions.

topicGaps: Verified open recordings now total 22.318333 h, still 13.681667 h below the 36-hour floor; this is an observed-duration ledger, not rendered hours or training equivalence.

New recordings improve AF/flutter, tachyarrhythmia ECG interpretation, and inherited-syndrome coverage. No newly verified long-form recording closes the gaps in antiarrhythmic pharmacology, bradycardia/syncope reasoning, pacing/CRT/CIED follow-up, EP signal fundamentals, or safety/equity systems.

The residual 13.681667-hour requirement is not feasible to claim as completed from the public recordings verified in this pass.
