practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional teaching diagram, which change most directly shortens the excitable gap that can sustain re-entry?

options.text: Longer effective refractory period in the circuit
Greater dispersion of refractoriness and a shorter refractory period in part of the circuit
Elimination of all autonomic input
A wider QRS alone

practiceQuestions.rationale: Re-entry reasoning depends on conduction, refractoriness, and heterogeneous tissue properties. The option describes conditions that can facilitate re-entry; it is a mechanism concept, not a patient-management rule.
practiceQuestions.domain: Basic Physiology, Anatomy, Pharmacology, and Genetics

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional ambulatory tracing shows irregular signal deflections during vigorous movement, but the person’s symptoms occurred later. What is the most defensible next interpretation?

options.text: The tracing proves atrial fibrillation caused the symptoms
The finding may be artifact or an unrelated rhythm observation; symptom–rhythm correlation and data quality matter
An ablation is indicated from this tracing
No further clinical evaluation can ever be useful

practiceQuestions.rationale: Artifact recognition, monitoring, and symptom–rhythm correlation are explicit CCEP topics. An isolated wearable observation cannot establish causality.

practiceQuestions.stem: During a fictional EP conference, a regular narrow tachycardia has VA timing findings that make an SVT mechanism uncertain. Which statement is best?

options.text: One intracardiac timing relationship always proves AVNRT
Mechanism should be integrated from rhythm data and maneuvers, with recognition of limitations and alternatives
All regular narrow tachycardias are accessory-pathway tachycardias
Surface ECG is never useful

practiceQuestions.rationale: The blueprint assesses EP-study interpretation across AVNRT, accessory pathways, and multiple SVT mechanisms. A single finding may be supportive rather than definitive.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which ABIM CCEP certification-blueprint category has the largest listed weight for a typical January 2026 certification examination?

options.text: Clinical Arrhythmias: Atrial, 12%
Devices, 20%
Clinical Arrhythmias: Supraventricular Tachycardias, 15%
Clinical Scenarios and Syndromes, 8%

practiceQuestions.rationale: The published blueprint lists Devices at 20%; Basic Physiology, Anatomy, Pharmacology, and Genetics is also 20%, but it is not an option. This is a public blueprint fact, not recalled exam content.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has syncope with no documented rhythm during symptoms. Which principle is most consistent with the ACC/AHA/HRS syncope guideline?

options.text: Use targeted testing selected by history, examination, and ECG context
Order every possible test before taking a history
Assume an arrhythmia is proven by syncope alone
Ignore cardiovascular history

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline centers initial evaluation on history, physical examination, and ECG, and supports selective rather than indiscriminate testing.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional learner sees a close pace-map match to a PVC morphology. What is the safest interpretation?

options.text: It by itself proves a procedure is safe and successful
It is one localization clue whose validity depends on pacing conditions, anatomy, and the full mapping context
It excludes all alternative sites
It replaces informed consent

practiceQuestions.rationale: Pace mapping is a CCEP core/ventricular concept but has recognized technical and anatomic limitations. It cannot establish procedural competence or safety alone.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best reflects the 2023 AF guideline’s scope for an educational case discussion?

options.text: AF management is limited to rhythm procedures
The guideline covers thromboembolic risk, anticoagulation, LAAO, ablation, and risk-factor modification among other areas
The guideline allows a course to prescribe for an individual
Stroke prevention has no role in AF

practiceQuestions.rationale: The HRS summary states that the guideline includes these domains. Applying them to a person still requires individualized clinical judgment.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional device patient may have lead infection or malfunction. Which boundary is most appropriate for this course?

options.text: Teach a home extraction technique
Use the scenario to identify urgent specialist evaluation and the need for an appropriately equipped extraction team when relevant
Guarantee that every lead should be abandoned
Ignore possible complications

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2026 consensus emphasizes selection, risk–benefit assessment, procedural planning, experienced teams, surgical backup, and serious potential complications.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional patient with a pacing indication and heart-failure context, what does “cardiac physiologic pacing” include in the 2023 HRS/APHRS/LAHRS guideline framing?

options.text: Only a single historical pacemaker mode
Strategies including CRT and conduction-system pacing intended to restore or preserve ventricular synchrony
A nonclinical wellness intervention only
A guarantee of improved outcomes for every individual

practiceQuestions.rationale: The HRS guideline describes cardiac physiologic pacing as including CRT and conduction-system pacing in patients with pacemaker indications or heart failure; candidacy remains individualized.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional competitive athlete has exertional palpitations and a concerning family history. What is the most appropriate course-level response?

options.text: Issue return-to-play clearance from the course
Frame an athlete-specific evaluation and specialist/shared-decision question set, recognizing that clearance requires clinical assessment
Assume all athlete ECG changes are benign
Ignore family history

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2024 HRS consensus emphasizes athlete-specific evaluation, risk stratification, treatment considerations, and shared decision-making. This course cannot clear an athlete.

title: Interventional Cardiology Training Program

prerequisites.level: Advanced postgraduate medical-learning plan for physicians/fellows with prior cardiovascular-disease knowledge; not entry-level, procedural, or patient-specific training.
prerequisites.formalBoundary: Formal fellowship and ABIM prerequisites are governed by the accredited programme and ABIM, not this course. No participant may perform, prescribe, interpret clinical images for care, or apply a case plan without appropriate license, privileges, supervision, and local policy.

objectives: Make evidence-aware, patient-centered case-selection arguments for coronary and structural disease.
Interpret the roles and limitations of angiography, coronary physiology, and intravascular imaging.
Recognize complex coronary lesion subsets and their complication-planning implications.
Describe ACS, shock, bleeding, radiation, and access safety as systems/team concerns.
Map learning to the public January 2026 ABIM blueprint without using proprietary or leaked examination content.
Critically appraise trials, registries, device evidence, quality metrics, and guideline updates.
Articulate structural-heart selection and Heart-Team principles.
State the exact limits of self-study relative to accredited fellowship, procedure credit, and ABIM certification.

units.title: Case selection, chronic coronary disease, and the Heart Team
objectives: Distinguish diagnostic evaluation, medical therapy, PCI, and surgical referral as conceptual options in chronic coronary disease.
Frame anatomy, technical feasibility, comorbidity, patient goals, and equity in a Heart-Team decision rather than treating angiographic stenosis alone.
Interpret how randomized trials, registries, and appropriateness/quality concepts inform a case discussion.
boardDomains: Miscellaneous—Procedure-related data and Quality of care (6%)
units.casePractice: Use a fictionalized left-main/multivessel vignette to make a one-page Heart-Team referral question. Do not recommend a procedure for a real person.
units.assessment: Five-item evidence-to-decision worksheet; cite a guideline statement and name missing patient-preference/operative-risk information.

units.title: Angiographic anatomy, access, contrast, and fluoroscopic safety
objectives: Identify the information required to describe coronary anatomy, dominance, ostial/anomalous features, and angiographic flow without attempting a procedure.
Explain why access choice, contrast risk, and radiation/occupational safety are pre-procedure systems issues.
Recognize that device selection, arterial access, and radiation exposure require local protocols, supervision, and authorised clinical roles.
units.casePractice: Link-only review of the normal DSA case; label coronary branches and list the non-image information required before an invasive plan.
units.assessment: Annotated anatomy and safety checklist; formative only and not a procedure competency assessment.

units.title: Coronary physiology and intracoronary imaging
objectives: Compare what angiography, pressure/flow indices, IVUS, and OCT can and cannot add to lesion assessment.
Interpret physiology/imaging as evidence integrated with symptoms, anatomy, and clinical context rather than a stand-alone treatment command.
Describe sources of discordance and uncertainty in left-main and bifurcation assessment.
boardDomains: Cardiac Imaging and Assessment—Diagnostic coronary imaging (9%)
units.casePractice: From a published or fictional de-identified vignette, make a modality-to-question table; do not calculate a treatment plan.
units.assessment: Six single-best-answer interpretation questions plus a limitation statement for each modality.

units.title: Acute coronary syndromes, shock, and escalation systems
objectives: Organize STEMI, NSTEMI, and unstable-angina evaluation around contemporary guideline scope and systems of care.
Recognize cardiogenic-shock staging as a communication/risk framework, not a substitute for a multidisciplinary emergency assessment.
Identify the educational boundaries of mechanical circulatory support, reperfusion, thrombectomy, and escalation decisions.
boardDomains: Case Selection and Management—UA/NSTEMI, STEMI, STEMI complications (20%)
units.casePractice: Run a fictional team handoff: identify hemodynamic status, unknowns, escalation contacts, and reasons not to undertake solo action.
units.assessment: Time-critical communication rubric and a 10-question post-video quiz.

units.title: Complex coronary PCI reasoning: left main, bifurcation, ostial disease, and CTO
objectives: Classify lesion features that make left-main, bifurcation, ostial, or chronic-total-occlusion cases complex.
Explain why case selection, imaging/physiology, surgical alternatives, and complication planning precede technical strategy.
Describe common technical troubleshooting concepts at a high level without presenting this self-study as procedural instruction.
units.casePractice: Compare two fictional anatomic summaries and write which missing variables should go to a Heart Team/supervisor before strategy selection.
units.assessment: Structured case conference note, assessed for reasoning and safety language—not technical execution.

units.title: Calcification, restenosis, drug-coated balloons, and advanced lesion subsets
objectives: Describe why coronary calcium and stent failure change lesion assessment and risk.
Summarize the SCAI consensus emphasis on intravascular imaging when feasible for calcified lesions.
Recognize that atherectomy, lithotripsy, DCBs, and CTO techniques require device-specific training, governance, and supervised competence.
units.casePractice: Use a fictional lesion description to list image-based questions, potential complications, and decision stakeholders; no device recipe.
units.assessment: Evidence table distinguishing a consensus recommendation, a device claim, and an unanswered question.

units.title: Complications, bleeding, and post-procedure safety
objectives: Recognize coronary, access-site, bleeding, embolic, perforation, no-reflow, and tamponade complication categories.
Explain the importance of emergency surgical pathways, multidisciplinary response, documentation, and post-procedure follow-up.
Relate antiplatelet/antithrombotic choices to bleeding–ischemia trade-offs and current guidelines rather than rote rules.
units.casePractice: Create a fictional M&M timeline focused on detection, communication, escalation, and documentation; do not assign bedside treatment steps.
units.assessment: Safety-event root-cause worksheet and reflection on supervision/escalation.

units.title: Structural and valvular intervention: selection, imaging, and longitudinal care
objectives: Describe the Hopkins-published second-year structural exposure as an institutional description, not a publicly verified separate accreditation/board pathway.
Apply the guideline principle that severe valve disease considered for intervention is assessed by a multidisciplinary Heart Valve Team.
Compare high-level selection, imaging, access, durability, coronary-access, conduction, and follow-up considerations in transcatheter valve care.
boardDomains: Catheter-Based Management of Noncoronary Disease—structural/valvular case selection (13%)
units.casePractice: Write a fictional valve-team referral summary that separates anatomy, symptoms, life expectancy, patient goals, and unanswered surgical-risk questions.
units.assessment: Multidisciplinary-case rubric; no learner receives credit for a structural procedure.

units.title: Pharmacology, anticoagulation, and peri-/post-intervention follow-up
objectives: Organize antiplatelets, anticoagulants, vasopressors/inotropes, contrast reactions, and post-intervention medicines by mechanism, indication context, and risk.

units.title: Quality, consent, research literacy, and professional limits
objectives: Interpret quality metrics, adverse-event reporting, device surveillance, registries, and trial results at a conceptual level.

boardDomains: Miscellaneous—ethical/legal issues, procedure-related data, quality of care (6%)
All ABIM domains through clinical judgment
units.casePractice: Appraise a fictional registry summary for selection bias, outcome definition, equity implications, and whether it can change local practice alone.
units.assessment: Evidence-appraisal memo and an explicit scope/limitations statement.

assignment.title: Supervised-discussion portfolio: evidence-to-decision and safety
deliverables: A fictional or lawfully linked de-identified case summary with a clinical question and a missing-information list.
A two-page evidence appraisal comparing one guideline/consensus source with one trial/registry claim.
A Heart-Team/safety escalation map that includes uncertainty, supervision, and follow-up.
A radiation/occupational-safety and documentation checklist.
assignment.gradingBoundary: Assess reasoning, source use, uncertainty, and safety communication only. Do not assess catheter manipulation, image-sign-off, prescription, or real-patient management. This is not a substitute for ACGME milestones or ABIM programme-director evaluations.

assessment.summativePlan: 30-question original single-best-answer knowledge check; portfolio rubric (case selection 30%, evidence/limitations 25%, safety/ethics 25%, communication/quality 20%).
assessment.nonClaims: No score predicts ABIM performance or clinical competence. No proprietary exam content, confidential case, or protected image is used.

studyHours.note: The 36-hour video floor is met by observed public recordings. Planned original clips are not rendered, uploaded, or counted.

mapping.institution: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine / The Johns Hopkins Hospital
mapping.name: Interventional Cardiology Training Program
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: The supplied official fellowship directory labels this an ACGME-accredited, 1-year program at The Johns Hopkins Hospital. Its linked current detail page describes a two-year organization: year 1 coronary intervention, mechanical circulatory support, diagnostic-catheterization refinement, shock-team/ECPR participation; year 2 structural interventions (TAVR, TMVR, M-TEER, T-TEER, TTVR, PFO/ASD closure, LAAO, alcohol septal ablation) and a weekly structural clinic. It lists M&M/education case-film review, journal club/QI discussion, research conference, ECG/echo/subspecialty conferences, cardiology grand rounds, cardiac-surgery case conference, and monthly journal clubs. It names Johns Hopkins Hospital as the principal site and says affiliated community sites may provide additional instruction, but does not publish a rotation calendar, confidential case logs, total didactic hours, individual competency decisions, or a separately accredited structural-heart fellowship.

unitMap.text: Case selection, chronic coronary disease, and the Heart Team
Angiographic anatomy, access, contrast, and fluoroscopic safety
Coronary physiology and intracoronary imaging
Acute coronary syndromes, shock, and escalation systems
Complex coronary PCI reasoning: left main, bifurcation, ostial disease, and CTO
Calcification, restenosis, drug-coated balloons, and advanced lesion subsets
Complications, bleeding, and post-procedure safety
Structural and valvular intervention: selection, imaging, and longitudinal care
Pharmacology, anticoagulation, and peri-/post-intervention follow-up
Quality, consent, research literacy, and professional limits

topicGaps: The verified 36.3217 hours are heavily weighted to left-main/bifurcation/calcified PCI and TAVI; fewer complete free recordings specifically cover access/closure complications, radiation physics, invasive hemodynamics, peri-/post-PCI pharmacology, peripheral intervention, and the full noncoronary structural spectrum.

boardNames: American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) — Interventional Cardiology Certification Examination
medical.boardStatus: ABIM offers a separate Interventional Cardiology Certification Examination and publishes a January 2026 certification blueprint. ACGME is the programme accreditor, not a certifying board. No independent-study course confers board status.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: ABIM policy checked 2026-10-07: at application, a physician must already be ABIM-certified in cardiovascular disease; complete required accredited training; demonstrate clinical/procedural competence and ethical behavior; hold a valid, unrestricted, unchallenged medical license; and pass the ABIM examination. The training pathway requires 12 months of accredited full-time interventional-cardiology fellowship in addition to three years of accredited cardiovascular-disease training. ABIM also requires at least 250 documented therapeutic interventional cardiac procedures during training, programme-director attestation, and defined planning/critical-manipulation/post-procedure/supervision participation. This study supplies none of those elements and does not create eligibility, licensure, credentialing, procedure credit, or a guarantee of passing.

officialProgrammes.name: Interventional Cardiology Training Program
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: The supplied official fellowship directory labels this an ACGME-accredited, 1-year program at The Johns Hopkins Hospital. Its linked current detail page describes a two-year organization: year 1 coronary intervention, mechanical circulatory support, diagnostic-catheterization refinement, shock-team/ECPR participation; year 2 structural interventions (TAVR, TMVR, M-TEER, T-TEER, TTVR, PFO/ASD closure, LAAO, alcohol septal ablation) and a weekly structural clinic. It lists M&M/education case-film review, journal club/QI discussion, research conference, ECG/echo/subspecialty conferences, cardiology grand rounds, cardiac-surgery case conference, and monthly journal clubs. It names Johns Hopkins Hospital as the principal site and says affiliated community sites may provide additional instruction, but does not publish a rotation calendar, confidential case logs, total didactic hours, individual competency decisions, or a separately accredited structural-heart fellowship.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The named Hopkins programme is real, not a directory category. Source identity is retained: the directory page says 1 year and ACGME accredited; the detailed Hopkins page says two years and describes an institutional structural second year. Current national ACGME requirements say an interventional-cardiology programme must be 12 months. This entry does not reconcile those documents, infer a separate accredited structural credential, or represent the detailed institutional page as ABIM eligibility proof.
sourceCaveats: Source conflict retained rather than resolved: Hopkins directory says 1 year and ACGME-accredited; Hopkins detail page calls the programme two years; current ACGME national requirement says 12 months. Confirm programme structure/accreditation directly with Hopkins/ACGME before relying on it.
ABIM eligibility and exam policies can change and are determined at application; the current policy, not this course, governs.

Most recordings are society/provider webinars, not Hopkins lectures. Brand/device/trial discussions require conflict-of-interest awareness and primary-source cross-checking.

This independent study is unaffiliated with Johns Hopkins, ABIM, ACGME, ACC/AHA, SCAI, PCR, or any lecture provider. practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional stable patient has significant left-main coronary disease and the optimal revascularization approach is uncertain after initial evaluation. Which next framing best reflects the 2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI guideline perspective?

options.text: Choose PCI solely from the angiographic image.
Use a multidisciplinary Heart Team and shared decision-making that incorporates goals and relevant clinical/anatomic context.
Defer all discussion of surgery until after PCI.
Use a single risk score as the only determinant.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline key perspectives recommend a Heart Team and patient-centered shared decision-making when the optimal revascularization strategy is unclear. This is a reasoning question, not treatment advice for any real patient.

practiceQuestions.stem: According to the ABIM eligibility policy, which condition is required for an interventional cardiology fellow to receive credit for a therapeutic interventional cardiac procedure toward the training pathway?

options.text: Being present in the room while another fellow is primary operator.
Reviewing a video of the case afterward.
Participating in planning, performing critical technical manipulations, being substantially involved in post-procedure management, and faculty supervision.
Documenting any diagnostic angiogram as a therapeutic procedure.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM specifies all four elements and permits only one fellow to receive credit per case. This course cannot supply or attest to cases.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional calcified coronary lesion is being discussed in a conference. Which statement is most consistent with the 2024 SCAI calcified-lesion consensus summary?

options.text: Angiography alone always determines calcium-modification choice.
Intravascular imaging should be used whenever feasible to determine calcium-modification strategy and vessel preparation.
Every calcified lesion should receive the same device.
Calcification has no implications for PCI risk.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SCAI’s summary recommends intravascular imaging whenever feasible for assessment and preparation in calcified CAD; device use remains context- and competence-dependent.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with ACS is planned for PCI. Which access-related statement is reflected in the 2021 revascularization guideline key perspectives?

options.text: Femoral access is always preferred.
Radial access is recommended in PCI for ACS or stable ischemic heart disease to reduce bleeding and vascular complications compared with femoral access.
Access choice has no relationship to complications.
Access selection is outside interventional cardiology practice.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The cited guideline identifies radial access as recommended to reduce bleeding and vascular complications. Actual access selection requires patient-specific assessment and trained operators.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which item is explicitly part of the January 2026 ABIM Interventional Cardiology certification blueprint?

options.text: Catheter-Based Management of Noncoronary Disease, including structural/valvular case selection.
Pediatric cardiac surgery as a primary domain.
Nuclear-medicine radiopharmaceutical therapy.
Dermatologic surgery.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The published blueprint assigns 13% to catheter-based noncoronary disease and names structural/valvular evaluation and case selection.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional severe valvular-heart-disease case is being considered for intervention. What does the ACC/AHA valve-guideline perspective require before choosing an intervention pathway?

options.text: A single operator decides without consultation.
Evaluation by a multidisciplinary Heart Valve Team.
Automatic TAVI for every patient.
No consideration of symptoms or life expectancy.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline recommends a multidisciplinary Heart Valve Team for all patients with severe valve disease being considered for intervention.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the ABIM training pathway for Interventional Cardiology certification as published in the current policy?

options.text: A video course alone satisfies the pathway.
It requires 12 months of accredited full-time interventional cardiology fellowship in addition to three years of accredited cardiovascular disease training, plus other ABIM requirements.
It requires no prior cardiovascular disease certification.
It is granted by ACGME after 36 lecture hours.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM requires prior cardiovascular disease certification at application, accredited training, licensure, competence verification, required procedures, and a passing exam. ACGME accredits programs; it does not confer individual board certification.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional cath-lab quality review identifies cumulative occupational radiation and musculoskeletal risk. Which approach best aligns with SCAI’s current resource center?

options.text: Ignore exposure because only patients are affected.
Use ALARA+/ergonomic and protective strategies as a team safety and quality issue.
Rely only on an individual operator’s memory.
Eliminate documentation of exposure.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SCAI frames occupational radiation and musculoskeletal hazards as lifelong risks and promotes ALARA+ plus practical protection and workflow strategies.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the most defensible way to use FFR/iFR, IVUS, or OCT in a fictional ambiguous coronary-lesion discussion?

options.text: Treat any single metric as a universal substitute for clinical judgment.
Integrate the modality’s result and limitations with angiography, anatomy, symptoms, and the clinical question.
Ignore device limitations and discordance.
Use imaging only after a complication.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABIM blueprint includes these modalities, and SCAI describes adjunctive intracoronary techniques as supplementing angiography in specific lesion subsets and clinical circumstances.

practiceQuestions.stem: For a fictional stable-ischemic-heart-disease patient after PCI, which statement is a faithful high-level summary of the 2021 revascularization guideline perspective on antiplatelet duration?

options.text: Every patient has the same fixed duration without regard to risk.
After considering recurrent ischemia and bleeding risks, select patients may transition to P2Y12-inhibitor monotherapy and stop aspirin after 1–3 months of DAPT.
Antiplatelet risk assessment is never necessary.
The guideline eliminates clinician follow-up.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The cited perspective states that short DAPT may be reasonable in select stable-ischemic patients after consideration of ischemic and bleeding risks. This is educational only; current individual decisions require the treating team and current local guidance.

title: Neurovascular Surgery Fellowship

prerequisites.courseLevel: Advanced independent study for physicians/trainees with prior neuroscience, neuroimaging, stroke, and neurosurgery/neurointervention foundations. It is not an entry-level procedural course.
knowledge: clinical evidence appraisal and professional ethics
skills: Ability to read guideline summaries critically
ability to participate in supervised multidisciplinary case discussion

prerequisites.officialBIDMCAdmissionBoundary: BIDMC states that applicants should have satisfactory ACGME-accredited (or Canadian equivalent) neurological-surgery residency/training or be senior residents in an accredited neurosurgery program with broad exposure and ICU experience. Some prior endovascular experience is beneficial; the page notes many applicants had completed 100 diagnostic cerebral angiograms. This is an admission description, not a self-study prerequisite or a certification standard.
prerequisites.safetyBoundary: Procedural learning requires institutional credentialing, supervision, simulation, radiation authorization, local policy, and real clinical training. None is supplied here.

objectives: Use a structured, source-cited vocabulary for neurovascular anatomy, multimodal imaging, lesion architecture, uncertainty, and multidisciplinary alternatives.
Appraise current AHA/ASA guideline summaries and distinguish them from older recorded technical discussion.
Describe, at a conceptual level, diagnostic angiography, radiation safety, acute ischemic stroke systems, aneurysm/aSAH, ICH, AVM/dAVF, and revascularization.
Recognize the limits of videos, cases, and independent study; identify when direct expert, ICU, stroke, neurosurgical, or interventional review is required.
Apply copyright, de-identification, conflict-of-interest, and non-rehosting rules when using authentic case resources.

Use anatomy as a decision-support description, not as a substitute for supervised interpretation.

medical.trackType: Clinical physician fellowship (actual BIDMC programme; independent-study course is not the fellowship)
boardNames: American Board of Neurological Surgery (ABNS) initial certification
Recognition of Focused Practice Designation in Central Nervous System Endovascular Surgery (joint ABNS/ABR/ABPN RFPD)
medical.boardStatus: No separate ABMS board certification titled “Neurovascular Surgery Fellowship” was identified. BIDMC is an actual two-year fellowship and appears on CAST’s accredited Neuroendovascular fellowship list (NI1005), but fellowship completion is not itself ABNS certification or an automatic RFPD. The RFPD is a separate focused-practice designation jointly sponsored by ABNS, ABR, and ABPN.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent course confers no ABNS Board Eligibility, ABNS certification, RFPD eligibility, licensure, fluoroscopy/radiation authorization, hospital privileges, case-log credit, or procedural competency. ABNS Board Eligibility follows ACGME neurological-surgery residency and ABNS conditions. For an ABNS-certified neurosurgeon, the published RFPD post-fellowship pathway additionally requires ABNS certification, an ACGME or CAST CNS-endovascular fellowship, 100 consecutive post-fellowship endovascular cases, recent primary-operator procedure documentation, a written examination, and approved application; other specialties have their own stated pathways. Verify current rules directly with the boards.

officialProgrammes.institution: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (Harvard Medical School Teaching Hospital)
officialProgrammes.name: Endovascular & Operative Neurovascular Surgery Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: BIDMC describes a two-year clinical fellowship with one fellow selected per year, training in both endovascular and open operative neurovascular procedures. For a fellow without prior endovascular experience, the initial four-month interval is in the angiography suite; BIDMC then describes an 18-month interval combining weekly endovascular and open operative procedures. Typical weekly description: two days endovascular suite, two days neurosurgical OR, one clinic day, plus weekly neurovascular conference. These are clinical rotations and supervised activities, not lecture hours.

officialProgrammes.name: Neuroendovascular Surgery Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official directory-listed institutional variant; a full internal rotation or lecture curriculum was not verified in the directory discovery.

medical.programmeSourceScope: This is **not** a generic directory category: although the supplied packet called attention to a category-level possibility, the BIDMC destination page is a named, separately described fellowship with duration, applicant description, director, and clinical schedule. Its official title uses “Endovascular & Operative Neurovascular Surgery Fellowship,” while the directory/breadcrumb label is “Neurovascular Surgery.” Only BIDMC is treated as an institutional programme for this entry. Other institutions/channels in the lecture ledger are external educational sources, not BIDMC variants. CAST’s listing corroborates a Beth Israel Deaconess Neuroendovascular fellowship (NI1005) but does not publish BIDMC’s full operative curriculum or prove ACGME accreditation.
sourceCaveats: BIDMC’s public page gives a high-level fellowship description, not a complete lecture roster, procedure log, competency assessment, or current application packet.
CAST accreditation and ACGME accreditation are distinct; this record identifies CAST listing and does not infer separate ACGME accreditation from it.
YouTube availability, titles, and duration can change. Public channel metadata/watch-page observations support only the stated media durations and access state on the check date.
Older recordings are educational context, not current clinical direction; current AHA/ASA and CAST sources take precedence where they differ.
Authentic case links are linked only. Free viewing does not mean permission to copy, rehost, train AI, or use commercially.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement most accurately describes the BIDMC offering used as the institutional source for this entry?

options.text: It is only a generic directory category with no separate programme.
It is a two-year clinical fellowship in endovascular and open operative neurovascular procedures.
It is an ACGME neurologic-surgery residency.
It is a self-paced online certificate.

practiceQuestions.rationale: BIDMC’s page explicitly calls it a two-year clinical fellowship training both endovascular and open operative neurovascular procedures. It is therefore an actual programme, not merely a category page.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner completes every module in this independent-study course. Which claim is supported?

options.text: The learner is automatically eligible for the CNS Endovascular RFPD.
The learner has completed a clinical fellowship.
The learner may use the course as independent education but gains no certification, credentialing, or licensure status.
The learner can perform diagnostic angiography without supervision.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Independent study is not clinical training or credentialing. The RFPD page has separate board, fellowship, case, examination, and application requirements.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional aSAH conference, which framing best matches the 2023 AHA/ASA summary?

options.text: Choose a modality solely from aneurysm size.
Delay source evaluation until all medical complications resolve.
Promptly evaluate and secure the ruptured aneurysm; balance intervention risk with patient/aneurysm factors through experts in both surgical and endovascular treatment.
Use prophylactic hypervolemia for all patients.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The summary recommends prompt evaluation/treatment, preferably within 24 hours, and specialist choice balancing risk; it advises against prophylactic hemodynamic augmentation and hypervolemia.

practiceQuestions.stem: According to the 2026 AHA/ASA AIS summary, which statement is correct?

options.text: EVT is never considered in larger ischemic cores.
EVT has a strong recommendation for basilar-artery occlusion within 24 hours when NIHSS is at least 10.
Intensive systolic BP lowering below 140 mm Hg after complete reperfusion is recommended for everyone.
All low-NIHSS patients should receive thrombolysis regardless of disability.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2026 summary reports a strong recommendation for that basilar-occlusion population. It also says intensive SBP lowering below 140 after EVT is not recommended and distinguishes non-disabling deficits.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has spontaneous ICH and no seizures. Which statement reflects the 2022 AHA/ASA summary?

options.text: Prophylactic antiseizure medication improves long-term functional outcome in all cases.
Platelet transfusion is helpful in all antiplatelet-associated ICH.

Etiologic assessment should consider microvascular and macrovascular causes; prophylactic antiseizure medication without evidence of seizures does not improve long-term seizure control or functional outcome.
Early aggressive mobilization in the first 24 hours improves mortality.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline summary emphasizes etiologic markers and states prophylactic antiseizure medication without seizures does not improve long-term outcomes. It also warns that platelet transfusion outside emergency surgery/severe thrombocytopenia may worsen outcome.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which feature is explicitly part of the CAST prerequisite neuroendovascular curriculum?

options.text: Independent unsupervised angiography after an online lecture.
Radiation physics, biology, and safety, plus interpretation of cerebral angiography and neurovascular studies.
A guarantee of ABNS RFPD eligibility.
Only open microsurgery; no imaging or critical care content.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CAST explicitly lists those elements, alongside catheter/contrast fundamentals, pathophysiology, coagulation, and acute vascular critical care.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best represents the current AHA bAVM statement’s scope?

options.text: Every incidental bAVM requires immediate intervention.
bAVMs are uncommon lesions that may present with hemorrhage, seizures, or headache, and the statement addresses natural history and treatment of ruptured and unruptured lesions.
AVM and dAVF are interchangeable terms.
The statement replaces multidisciplinary review.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AHA page describes bAVMs as uncommon and notes hemorrhage, seizures, headache, incidental discovery, and review of natural history/treatment. It does not make a universal treatment rule.

practiceQuestions.stem: You want to show an authentic Radiopaedia neurovascular case in a free, noncommercial teaching discussion. What is required?

options.text: No attribution is needed because the case is publicly viewable.
Attribute the contributor, Radiopaedia.org, and rID; preserve noncommercial/share-alike conditions and do not assume paid or paywalled use is permitted.
Download and rehost the full case in any app.
Convert the case into a synthetic diagnostic image without disclosure.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Radiopaedia states its cases are CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 and gives explicit attribution requirements. Public viewing is not unrestricted commercial re-use.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which description of MedPix is best supported by the NLM Data.gov record?

options.text: A proprietary test bank that must be copied into a course.
A public NLM database of patient cases integrating images and textual information, organized by clinical and image metadata.
A source of synthetic diagnostic images.
A substitute for local clinical records.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The NLM Data.gov record describes MedPix as a public database of patient cases integrating images and textual information. It also describes submission of de-identified images. Use linked cases under their native terms; do not treat them as a clinical record or rehost them.

practiceQuestions.stem: Why does this course label CAST requirements as a curriculum crosswalk rather than an official board-exam blueprint?

options.text: CAST requirements are irrelevant to neuroendovascular learning.
The published CAST document describes fellowship curriculum and case/training requirements, while no public ABNS RFPD item-by-item exam blueprint was identified.
The course has access to proprietary ABNS test questions.
Any lecture series automatically creates a board blueprint.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Training requirements and a credential examination are different source types. This course uses the public CAST curriculum transparently and does not claim access to proprietary examination content.
